body:
# Worker turns ending prematurely mid-step force orch re-dispatch (preview no-op + ping termination)

Related: #353 (loop-session wedge + resume no-op). This issue covers two more
premature-turn failures in the same run that forced the orchestrator to
cancel/re-dispatch mid-step work.

## Instance 1 ΓÇö Step 5 verify dispatched, did nothing (preview-only no-op)

- Dispatched `ws-plan-verify` (Step 5) with full context pointers + VerboseMode addendum.
- Child `01a0b6f5-ced1-73a1-82c8-36a43f5ef7bb`
  (`subagent/01a0b6f5-cee0-7122-b787-37946ebf97e9/session.jsonl`): **44 log lines,
  1 model turn, 0 tool calls**. Entire output was the `Starting step 5 (Verify):`
  preview; no spec/ledger reads, no tests, no `step-05-*.plan.report.md`.
- Orchestrator detected the missing report artifact and re-dispatched a fresh
  worker with an explicit structural rule ("complete verification AND write the
  report in this turn; preview without work is failed delivery").
- Retry child `01a0b6f6-9db2-7fa1-aedd-294d622dd9b4` ran ~15 min and scored 9/10.
- Cost: one wasted dispatch + ~15 min of wall time before the retry even started
  producing (detection was artifact-based, not signaled).

## Instance 2 ΓÇö batch-3 fix worker terminated by a parent status ping

- Batch-3 worker `01a0b75f-6d3e-7650-bd98-881d10303b37` was mid-batch after ~20 min
  (46 model turns of real work: 30 bash, 31 reads, 13 edits; fixes + tests
  implemented, full suite mid-verification, no push/report yet).
- Parent sent a queue-mode status ping (`baton-batch3-ping`, asking for activity + ETA).
- Ping arrived at worker log seq 1817 of 1835
  (`subagent/01a0b75f-6d53-7a22-9069-866b88155afa/session.jsonl`). The worker's
  **next message ΓÇö a status reply ("Remaining: ΓÇª ETA ~10 min. No blocker.") ΓÇö
  became its terminal output**: `terminal` + `completed` follow immediately,
  with no further tool calls. No push, no round report, fixes left uncommitted.
- A continuation worker (`01a0b773-a160-7610-913a-70bae9df7e58`) verified,
  committed `c4b66bfd`, resolved, pushed, and reported from the intact worktree.
- Cost: one extra dispatch; parent now avoids pinging workers mid-batch entirely
  (batches 4ΓÇô7 ran unpinged with no recurrence).

## Impact

- Every premature turn costs a full re-dispatch (context rebuild + repeated reads)
  and, worse, is silent: the parent only notices via missing artifacts or
  elapsed time, never via an explicit failure signal.
- Pings ΓÇö the only liveness probe the parent has ΓÇö can themselves kill the turn
  they probe, removing the probe as an option.
- Same run also hit the loop-session wedge + resume no-op (#353), so 4 of ~15
  dispatches in one run ended prematurely in three different ways.

## Suspected causes (to investigate)

1. **Preview-then-yield:** the VerboseMode "print preview before any tool call"
   instruction keeps inducing turn end right after the preview (5th instance
   counting #353), even with explicit structural mandates to continue.
2. **Ping-as-final-message:** a queued status message delivered late in a long
   worker turn appears to be treated as a prompt to *respond and finish*
   rather than *acknowledge and continue*. Possibly the model interprets any
   parent message as a new terminal request, or the runtime closes the turn
   after the next assistant message post-interrupt.
3. **No failure signal:** both cases resolved as `completed` (or ready-with-text),
   so the parent cannot distinguish "done" from "gave up" without artifact checks.

## Follow-ups

- [ ] Harden the VerboseMode addendum (shared with #353): mandate tool calls in
      the same response; never end the turn after the preview.
- [ ] Define a safe liveness probe for long workers that cannot terminate the
      turn (read-only status poll), or document "never ping mid-batch" as the
      contract and give parents a non-messaging progress signal instead.
- [ ] Emit an explicit non-success signal when a worker ends with zero tool
      calls or with required artifacts unwritten, so parents can fail fast
      instead of waiting out full timeouts.
- [ ] Consider resuming (not re-dispatching) interrupted workers when the
      worktree already holds their partial progress.

## Environment

- Run: `step-baton-multi-agent-runs-20260918T232508Z`, PR #350 (merged `eee9fa49`)
- Package 0.4.38, Tier 1 `subagent_spawn`, models `muse-spark`
- Artifacts: `.agents/plans/step-baton-multi-agent-runs/runs/pr-350/round-3-*.md`,
  `.agents/codereviews/PR-350-round-3.md` (continuation), Step 5 report
  `step-05-step-baton-multi-agent-runs.plan.report.md` (retry)
title: Worker turns ending prematurely mid-step force orch re-dispatch (preview no-op + ping termination)
